items.title: FTC scam alert — fake agents call demanding payment, hang up and call 1-877-FTC-HELP
items.summary: Your caller ID says FTC. The voice sounds official, uses a real employee name, claims identity theft or recovered money. They need verification or a fee. The FTC does NOT cold-call, never demands gift cards/crypto/wire/gold, and has no badge agents. Hang up. Share nothing. If concerned, call FTC yourself at 1-877-FTC-HELP or visit ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.title: Firefox 153 ships Containers by default — separate Work, Personal, Banking, Shopping in one window free
items.summary: Open Firefox 153+, click the menu -> New Container Tab -> pick Work, Personal, Banking, or Shopping. Each Firefox Container has its own cookies, logins, and tracking - Google in your Work Container cannot see your Personal YouTube history. No extension needed; it is built in.

items.title: Run Llama 3.3 8B locally on 8GB RAM — Ollama + Open WebUI is free, offline, no account needed
items.summary: Install Ollama from ollama.com (Windows/macOS/Linux), then run 'ollama run llama3.3:8b' - that is a local model. For a chat UI, run 'docker run -d -p 3000:8080 -v open-webui:/app/backend/data ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main' and open localhost:3000. Your prompts never leave your machine.

items.title: ONYX SYSTEMS: TECH TIP — Harden Linux Kernel via sysctl: Set kptr_restrict=2, dmesg_restrict=1, mmap_rnd_bits=32
items.summary: Three sysctl knobs harden kernel info leaks and ASLR. Create /etc/sysctl.d/99-onx-hardening.conf with the three lines, run sudo sysctl --system. No reboot.

items.title: Your NVMe SSD is silently failing — smartctl reads its health free at the terminal
items.summary: Run `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0` (Linux) or install CrystalDiskInfo free at crystalmark.info (Windows) to see your SSD's real health — percentage used, temperature, and power-on hours. Most drives warn at 80% life used; I've seen drives die at 95% with zero Windows warnings.
